aidb_assessment.novelty: High conceptual novelty within the supplied literature framing: the paper turns prompt assembly after retrieval into an independently measurable multimodal-memory stage and uses matched controls to distinguish content, identity, time and binding from rendering confounds.
aidb_assessment.rationale: The central paired decomposition and component controls are strong enough to merit close reading and replication. Adoption should wait for released artifacts and validation on independent benchmarks, backbones, modalities and privacy-aware deployments. The strongest qualification is heterogeneity: delivery dominates MemLens under the reported protocol, but DMV-Bench on one backbone is overwhelmingly retrieval-limited, and assembled components can harm some question types.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: High for builders of multimodal memory agents that preserve original media. The interface changes are training-free and the diagnostic decomposition can identify whether retrieval, presentation or item selection is limiting performance. Utility is narrower for text-only stores, privacy-constrained deployments and modalities not evaluated here.

executive_summary: The paper isolates “delivery,” the post-retrieval transformation of stored multimodal records into prompt content. Its strongest evidence is a paired MemLens decomposition: with gold messages fixed, retaining pixels improves accuracy far more than replacing ordinary retrieval with oracle retrieval. DeliverMem preserves pixels, adds readable image identities and temporal annotations, and pairs these with region-aware retrieval. It leads published memory-agent baselines on MemLens and DMV-Bench, but effects are sharply task- and backbone-dependent. The controls are unusually careful; nevertheless, only image memory is tested, some headline comparisons use published rather than paired runs, and the promised code and outputs were not yet available in the supplied record.

assumptions: The benchmark judge is an adequate accuracy measure for MemLens; exact page selection is the appropriate success criterion for DMV-Bench.
The oracle condition—gold messages padded or truncated to the fixed delivery budget—meaningfully represents retrieval at ceiling for that budget.
Paired question-level sign tests on MemLens and chain-level permutation tests on DMV-Bench capture the relevant dependence structure.
The chosen delivery budgets and prompt interface are representative enough to support conclusions about post-retrieval delivery.
The original media and timestamps remain available in storage; D1–D3 cannot retrofit systems that discarded them during ingestion.
key_components: D1, original-modality preservation: retrieved records retain their pixels rather than being reduced to textual proxies.
D2, addressability: a short identifier is rendered into each delivered image and named in the accompanying prompt.
D3, temporal position: each item receives the finest available store index, using dates on MemLens and append ordinals on DMV-Bench.
R1, region multi-vector retrieval: whole-image and overlapping regional SigLIP 2 representations are combined using MaxSim.
Paired controls include withheld, decoy, phase-randomized and spatially scrambled images; constant, shuffled, absent and text-only tags; permuted or absent dates; and shuffled image-message binding.
method.overview: The authors formalize answering as a model conditioned on a delivered transformation of retrieved records. They estimate delivery and retrieval effects from paired conditions sharing questions, answering model, prompt template and judge. DeliverMem then modifies outgoing context without training: it retains original images, stamps each image with a readable tag referenced by the prompt, and attaches a timestamp or append ordinal. A separate retrieval adapter encodes each image globally and over an overlapping regional grid, scoring it by region MaxSim. Delivery components are evaluated against controls intended to preserve the delivered set, order and budget while changing one property.

open_questions: Do the delivery effects replicate with independently implemented prompts, retrievers and judges rather than the authors’ pipeline?
How should an agent choose between a crop, a full frame and both when evidence has region annotations?
Can content-preserving delivery work for audio and video while controlling duration, temporal alignment and cross-modal binding?
Would a privacy-filtered or selectively redacted delivery policy retain the accuracy gains of raw-pixel delivery?
Why does the assembled configuration harm knowledge-update and some information-extraction questions, and can routing avoid those losses without relying on benchmark-provided question types?
How stable are the results under repeated API calls, alternative judge models and non-Qwen open backbones?

problem.importance: A record may be retrieved successfully while decisive visual information is withheld or made hard to address. Such failures can be misdiagnosed as retrieval or reasoning failures, directing optimization toward the wrong stage.
problem.scope: The paper studies image-based long-term agent memory on MemLens and DMV-Bench. It separates delivery from retrieval, evaluates original-modality preservation, item identity, temporal position and image-message binding, and adds one region-aware retrieval adapter. It does not experimentally establish transfer to audio, video or other modalities.
problem.statement: Multimodal memory research usually optimizes storage and retrieval but does not isolate the interface that determines which parts of a retrieved record, and in which modality and structure, reach the answering model.

proposed_experiments.baseline: For a new benchmark with paired visually supported and text-supported questions over the same retrieved records, compare gold-set delivery with original images against identical delivery with pixels withheld and against phase-randomized images.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Original-modality delivery improves accuracy only when the requested fact is visually grounded, and does not improve matched text-supported questions.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Paired accuracy difference and the interaction between delivery condition and evidence type, with confidence intervals and multiplicity-corrected tests.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop after the preregistered sample provides enough discordant pairs for the target power; reject broad transfer if the interaction is absent or the visual subset fails to improve over both controls.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Compare the fixed DeliverMem configuration with a no-component baseline and a router trained only on a disjoint development split without benchmark-provided question labels.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Adaptive component routing preserves DeliverMem’s useful effects while eliminating losses on question types that do not need tags, dates or region retrieval.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Held-out macro accuracy across question types, accompanied by worst-type accuracy and the fraction of queries using each component.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop if the router fails to exceed the fixed configuration on macro accuracy or reduces any preregistered question type beyond the allowed non-inferiority margin.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Compare raw-pixel delivery, caption-only delivery, and automatically redacted or cropped delivery under an identical oracle retrieved set and prompt structure.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Privacy-filtered visual delivery retains most of the original-pixel benefit while exposing less sensitive image content.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Accuracy versus a preregistered privacy-exposure score based on retained sensitive regions, reported as a Pareto frontier.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop if no filtered condition improves accuracy over caption-only delivery while meeting the privacy threshold, or if it cannot retain the preregistered fraction of raw-pixel accuracy gain.

results.context: This is the paper’s central controlled decomposition. It supports a larger delivery opportunity under this exact benchmark, budget, judge and backbone, but not a universal ranking of stages.
results.result: On MemLens’s non-refusal subset, fixing the retrieved set to gold messages and retaining pixels yielded 43.93 accuracy versus 30.06 with pixels withheld, a +13.87 delivery effect. Replacing ordinary retrieval with gold retrieval while retaining pixels yielded only +2.31 and was not statistically distinguishable from zero; the paired delivery contrast was significant.

results.context: The direction replicates across tested backbones, but the comparative advantage narrows and the larger-backbone differences lack significance at the reported sample size.

results.result: Across three Qwen3-VL backbones, delivery remained larger than retrieval: +13.87 versus +2.31, +15.61 versus +9.83, and +17.92 versus +11.56. The delivery-to-retrieval ratio narrowed from 6.00× to 1.59× and 1.55×, while the between-term gap was significant only on the smallest backbone.

results.result: DeliverMem outperformed the best published MemLens memory agent at every released context length: scores were 51.28, 44.10, 42.05 and 38.97, with margins of +18.46, +12.82, +10.77 and +8.20. The reported full-context-to-delivered input ratios were 10.0×, 19.2×, 36.6× and 72.9×.

results.context: This demonstrates system-level strength but also limits the broad delivery claim: the DMV-Bench gain can be primarily retrieval-driven and depends on the backbone’s failure mode.

evidence.quote: Qwen2.5-VL-7B Gemini 2.5 Flash
The main effects are +22.16 for (R1), with all six chains agreeing in sign at the permutation floor p=0.031, and +0.46 for delivery at p=0.156.

results.result: On DMV-Bench, DeliverMem exceeded the published DualMem scores in all reported settings on both backbones, with margins ranging from +7.0 to +16.7 on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and from +10.6 to +23.5 on Gemini 2.5 Flash. Same-batch comparisons were also positive, but attribution differed: on Gemini at the heaviest setting, region retrieval had a +22.16 main effect while delivery had +0.46 and was non-significant.

results.context: The matched controls strengthen causal interpretation for individual interface properties, while the heterogeneous and adverse effects argue against treating every component as universally useful.

results.result: Component effects were specific rather than uniformly beneficial. Original image content contributed +11.56 on MemLens; accurate temporal position gained +13.92 on temporal questions; addressability gained +11.85 against a constant-tag control on DMV-Bench but only +0.51 on MemLens. The assembled tag-and-date change also harmed some question types.

title: Retrieved but Not Delivered: Multimodal Memory Delivery for Long-Term Agents

uncertainties.why_it_matters: Benchmark structure determines whether evidence is already retrieved, whether questions require pixels, and whether tags or dates supply missing information. These factors directly govern the measured effect.
